newsitem.title: CHAD: Chad ruling party closer to parliament majority.
newsitem.headline: Chad ruling party closer to parliament majority.

text.p: Chad's ruling party moved closer to a majority in the new 125-seat parliament, winning six seats in the capital in Sunday's second-round run-offs and taking its tally to 43, provisional results showed.

The results, released by the independent electoral commission in N'Djamena on Tuesday, showed that the other five seats on offer went to the opposition in the form of supporters of former prime minister Jean Bawoyeu Alingue.
Alingue cried fraud on Sunday, accusing officials of illegally handing out new voter cards on polling day.
The opposition Rally for Democracy and Progress (RDP) party said on Sunday that voter lists had been falsified.
Officials say a dozen RDP militants, including its leader, Mahamat Saleh Younouss, have been arrested and detained on charges of "trying to disrupt the smooth running of the poll".
Electoral officials predict final results in about 10 days.
Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement won 37 seats in the January 5 first round against a total of 20 for other parties.
Deby, a former guerrilla leader from the Moslem north, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup after decades of civil war or conflict with Libya.
After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential election in July in a runoff against fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue from the largely Christian south.
Chad, a sprawling former French colony on the fringes of the Sahara desert, previously had a 57-member interim assembly under a 1993 transitional charter.
